Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Depression severity was not correlated with serum vitamin D concentration in postmenopausal women.
Sentence: "No correlation of the depression severity with the serum vitamin D concentration or other criteria of metabolic syndrome was found."
Measured as: depression severity (Beck Depression Inventory)
Population: 396 postmenopausal women from rural and urban areas in the Lublin region, Poland
Intervention: Serum vitamin D concentration (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower vs higher serum vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 396
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficiency was associated with increased depressive symptoms in patients with severe mental illness.
Sentence: "Vitamin D deficiency was significantly associated with worse psychiatric outcomes, including increased depressive symptoms (adjusted OR = 1.89, p = 0.018), lower Global Assessment of Functioning scores (adjusted OR = -0.18, p < 0.001), and higher rates of metabolic syndrome (adjusted OR = 1.97, p = 0.007)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms
Population: 1003 patients with severe mental illnesses (schizophrenia, major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder)
Intervention: Vitamin D deficiency (serum level, observational exposure)
Comparator: Patients without vitamin D deficiency
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 1,003
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are cross-sectional vitamin D associations with depressive symptoms, but one found none in healthy postmenopausal women and the other found an association in patients with severe mental illness.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["outcome_measure","comparator"],"detail":"population: community postmenopausal women (n=396) vs psychiatric patients with schizophrenia, MDD or bipolar disorder (n=1,003); BDI continuous correlation vs deficiency-vs-no-deficiency odds ratio"}
